title: Silver jewellery for men: simple pieces to start with
description: New to silver jewellery for men? Start with a chain, a small pendant, a bracelet or kada and a plain ring. Sizes, thickness and mistakes to avoid, explained.
intro: If you are new to silver jewellery, start with one piece you can wear every day without thinking about it: a medium-weight silver chain, with or without a small pendant, is the easiest entry point for most men. Add a bracelet or kada next, and a plain ring after that. Building slowly lets you find what feels natural on you.

sections.heading: Why silver works well for men starting out
paragraphs: Silver has a cool, understated look that sits comfortably with both western and Indian clothing. It pairs with steel watches, grey and black clothes, denim and white kurtas without looking flashy. It also costs far less than gold, so trying a style and deciding it is not for you is not an expensive mistake.
Silver also has deep roots in Indian men's jewellery, from kadas to chains worn by grandfathers, so it rarely looks out of place at a family function.

sections.heading: Piece 1: A silver chain
paragraphs: A chain is the backbone of most men's jewellery. For a first chain, these points matter most:
list: Length: 20 to 22 inches suits most men, sitting at or just below the collarbone. Broader necks or a longer look may need 24 inches.
Thickness: roughly 2 to 4 mm looks substantial without being heavy. Very fine chains can look delicate; very thick ones read as a statement.
Style: curb, box and rope chains are durable and look masculine. Snake chains look sleek but kink if bent sharply.
Clasp: a lobster clasp is easier to use and more secure than a spring ring on heavier chains.

sections.heading: Piece 2: A small pendant
paragraphs: Once you are comfortable with a chain, a pendant adds personal meaning. Keep it modest, about the size of a thumbnail or a little larger, so it can be tucked under a shirt for office and worn out with a T-shirt on weekends.

Popular choices include plain geometric shapes, a simple cross or religious symbol, initials, or a single stone. Many men prefer devotional pendants. Varaha's [Divine collection](/divine) has Om, Trishul and Shiva pendants on Rudraksha mala chains; these are gold plated rather than silver, but are worth a look if you want something spiritual. For silver, the [925 sterling silver pendants](/silver) include simpler designs that can go on a man's chain too, as long as the bail fits it.

sections.heading: Piece 3: A bracelet or kada
paragraphs: A silver kada is a classic in many Indian households, especially in Sikh and Punjabi families, where it carries religious meaning. Even outside that tradition, a plain kada is a strong, simple piece that works with almost any outfit.

If you prefer something flexible, a chain-link bracelet in curb or box style is a good choice. Wear it on the wrist opposite your watch, or on the same wrist if you like a stacked look, though the watch case can scratch silver over time. For fit, you should be able to slip one finger between the bracelet and your wrist.

sections.heading: Piece 4: A plain ring
paragraphs: Rings take the most knocks of any jewellery, so start with a plain silver band without stones. A flat or slightly rounded band 4 to 6 mm wide suits most hands. Get your size measured at a jeweller, or measure a ring you already own, since fingers swell a little in summer and in the evening.
Silver rings scratch with use. Many men like the softened, slightly worn look that develops. If you want it to stay bright, a polishing cloth now and then is enough.

sections.heading: Common mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Wearing everything at once is the big one. A chain, a pendant, a kada, two rings and a bracelet can tip from stylish to cluttered quickly. Two or three pieces are plenty for most days.

The second is buying 'silver-coloured' steel or plated chains and expecting them to behave like silver. Look for a 925 or sterling stamp and ask the seller if unsure. The third is ignoring comfort. A chain that pulls on neck hair or a ring that pinches will end up in a drawer. Finally, take silver off for the gym and swimming. Sweat and chlorine both speed up tarnish.

faq.q: What length silver chain is best for men?
faq.a: 20 to 22 inches suits most men. Go to 24 inches if you want the pendant to sit lower on the chest or have a broader neck.

faq.q: Can men wear silver chains every day?
faq.a: Yes. Sterling silver is durable. Remove it for workouts, swimming and bathing to keep it bright longer.

faq.q: Is a silver kada good for daily wear?
faq.a: Yes, a solid kada is sturdy. It will pick up scratches over time, which many people like as part of its character.
